<description>
This doesn't fix the general case of rebroadcasting potentially surprising users by divulging the originator IP trivially, but for users opting into private broadcast, it seems a bridge too far for them to expect the current behavior.

e.g. an incoming dust payment triggering your node to rebroadcast 24-36th later over clearnet

This can be removed if/when wallet drives through private broadcast.

see https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/3828 for running broader issue
</description>

<new_statements>
[2026-10-09] c:6074151790 comment by vasild (member) (edited 2026-10-09):
* The wallet transactions are initially sent to all peers and periodically rebroadcast. This has not changed in 10 years and was not changed by the introduction of private broadcast. The wallet does not use private broadcast.

* The wallet rebroadcast is and has always been bad for privacy, but it has its use cases. This PR would cripple the wallet due to an unrelated feature being enabled.

* I see the idea here is to try to protect users that create transactions in the wallet, but do not broadcast them via the wallet and use `sendrawtransaction` RPC instead with private broadcast. For these users, that do not use the wallet initial send either, `-walletbroadcast=0` fits very well. I think this should be resolved via some communication channel to advise people of that.

Concept NACK
[2026-10-09] c:6081186947 comment by instagibbs (member):
[quoted text omitted]

Interactions between features exist and should not be ignored. It's a wallet issue, for sure, but for a wallet + pb user, it would be extremely surprising.

[quoted text omitted]
I don't think handing users footguns and hoping they read the docs is the right approach. Ideally we'd remove / replace rebroadcasts entirely, then this particular coupling can disappear safely. https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/36403#issuecomment-6051815930 for some discussion for those following at home.
[2026-10-09] c:6084798078 comment by polespinasa (member):
I tend to concept NACK this although I cannot come with a better proposal that 100% fixes this right now.

I don't think disallowing re-broadcast is the right solution (I know this is proposed as a temporal fix). Although it is not perfect, I prefer something like #36482 which I consider a good half-patch that limits this issue to a really specific case were a transaction disappears from node's mempool and is when we should consider rebroadcast necessary (in its current implementation).

I don't think the incoming dust privacy attack is an argument for pushing this PR forward. That attack affects both, private and standard broadcast, and as I understand private broadcast, it improves your privacy when you send a transaction, not when you receive one. It helps hiding you are the origin of a transaction, but that doesn't mean that it makes impossible to know that you are the origin of a transaction.
In other words, I think the dust-resubmit attack is worth fixing and we should fix it, but it is worth fixing for all cases, not only private broadcast. I don't feel disabling a useful feature such as rebroadcast is the right step here. We also shouldn't assume and say that private broadcast makes impossible to know the origin of a transaction, it does improve privacy and makes it more difficult and expensive to know.
</new_statements>
